## Topic and Research Question

- Traffic and car emissions are known to impact local air pollution and climate (Niemeier, et al. 2006)  
- Precipitation and temperature changes and an increase in storms are known indicators of climate change (Trenberth, 2007; EPA, 2024; Lindsey & Dahlman, 2025)
- Can we observe the varying impact of traffic congestion on climate between counties in Arizona, USA?
- Can we predict the impact of traffic congestion on climate?


## Data

-   Urbanization Metric: traffic count data (USDT FHA) 
-   Climate Metric: temperature, precipitation, and storm data (National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA))

## Set Up
- The three datasets were loaded, missing values were replaced or rows were removed, and any additional features were engineered.
- Function was created to transform lat/lon data into gridspace for grouping the data into grids.
- Once merged on gridspace and county code, the numeric features were normalized and categorical variables encoded, and data was fitted and transformed via feature scaling.
